messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: p99 latency spike detected on /v1/stream/generate (us-west2). p95=220ms, p99=2.5s over last 5m, streaming stalls observed. paging on-call. Severity: SEV2

sara: oncall here, looking. seeing sustained p99 > 2s and a tail of multi-second stalls on streaming clients (chunks stall then resume). tagging @harper for infra handoff.

harper: copying in. grabbing metrics and node map now. which nodes are hot?

maria: traces show KV cache misses spiking for long sequences, but there are also a cluster of kernel logs from gpunode-14 referencing ECC correctable errors and a thermal throttle event at 14:03:12.

jake: confirmed: gpunode-14 GPU0 had 4 correctable ECC events in 12m, then a thermal governor reduce clock to 70% around 14:03. That aligns with p99 spike.

eng-sre: CPU and disk fine. GPU metrics: power draw dropping, fan RPM oscillation, and GPU util falling during throttles. Also noticed continuous batching queue length temporarily doubled.

sara: impact assessment: streaming sessions in us-west2 (approx 2.4% of total sessions) saw stalls/reconnects. No total request loss but perceived latency for customers integrating streaming (websocket/frame stalls). support-lead, can you flag any customer pages?

support-lead: FYI support observed 3 customer tickets referencing chunking/long stalls in last 10m. Escalating to SRE for mitigation.

harper: mitigation plan: 1) immediate: cordon/drain gpunode-14 from runtime routing 2) route new streaming requests to us-west2 fallback pool (gpu-pool-b) with spare capacity 3) reduce max-batch-size for streaming router to avoid long queuing for now

maria: agree. also reduce contiguous sequence batching for sessions with >1024 tokens to limit prefix KV pressure.

jake: commands to run if approved:
```bash
# cordon and drain node (ignore daemonsets)
kubectl cordon gpunode-14
kubectl drain gpunode-14 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60
```

ops-bot: Runbooksuggest: apply realtime fallback policy: `route-policy streaming: fallback-to: gpu-pool-b threshold: p99>1.5s` — kicked off.

sara: executing drain now. will monitor p99 and streaming error rate. tagging @eng-sre for rollback hooks.

eng-sre: observed immediate partial recovery after marking node unschedulable — p99 dropped from 2.5s -> 700ms over 90s, streaming stall count down 82%. Good sign.

sara: continuing with drain. creating a short-term capacity bump on gpu-pool-b (allow bursting +20%).

harper: hardware follow-up: open ticket with vendor for ECC count and fan oscillation. suspect intermittent fan controller causing temp excursions. Put node into quarantine once drain completes.

maria: adding telemetry to surface per-GPU correctable ECC rate into alert dashboard (currently aggregated per-host). Want per-GPU thresholds to detect early flares.

support-lead: telling impacted customers we're seeing degraded streaming in us-west2, we've applied live mitigations and are routing traffic — ETA for full recovery ~15m.

jake: note: we saw a correlated bump in batch queue length for long-request workloads. We'll lower continuous-batch-window from 50ms -> 20ms for streaming route as a temporary SLO-preserving measure.

sara: handoff: @harper will take post-drain hardware checks and vendor ticket; @maria will own alert/dashboard changes; @jake will follow up with runtime config change and rollback plan; I will run the post-incident customer impact summary and link tickets. Next oncall in 30m (handing to @harper).

harper: on it. once drain completes I'll confirm quarantine and kick hardware ticket. also propose adding a short-term p99 mitigation that prefers replica pools with <2 ecc-correctable events in last 30m.

eng-sre: final state update: drain finished, node isolated, p99 stable ~600ms, streaming error rate returned to baseline. Will keep monitoring for 1h.

sara: SEV2 -> monitoring state. Creating incident board and postmortem template with action items: hardware ticket, per-GPU alerting, adjust continuous-batching heuristics, and customer comms follow-up.

support-lead: drafting customer note now. will include mitigation steps and next-steps for hardware replacement.

incident-bot: Incident status change: SEV2 -> MONITORING by sara at 14:35.

sara: closing handoff to @harper for follow-ups. if we see another thermal/ECC flare we'll reopen paging. thanks all :thumbsup:
